};

} // namespace errors

Holds the results of a completed command execution, including process ID, exit code, and captured standard error/output text. Supports background execution, event emission, working directory, initial stdin content, custom environment variables, and optional stdout/stderr streaming handlers. functions.name: helpers::split
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> helpers::split(const std::string &s, char delim, unsigned int stopAfter = (unsigned int)-1)
functions.description: Splits a string into substrings using a single-character delimiter. The optional stopAfter parameter limits how many splits are performed; when omitted, it defaults to no practical limit. Use to tokenize delimited input.
requirements: s may be any valid std::string (UTF-8 or other byte content accepted).
delim is a single char used as separator.
stopAfter is an unsigned count of splits to perform; behavior for specific values (e.g., 0) is not documented in the header.
Output order preserves the order of tokens in s. Other edge-case behaviors (e.g., consecutive delimiters, trailing delimiters) are unspecified in the header.

functions.name: helpers::splitTwo
functions.description: Splits a string into up to two parts around the first occurrence of a delimiter character. Intended for key/value or name/value style parsing.
requirements: s may be any valid std::string.
delim is a single char used as separator.
Exact output shape when the delimiter is absent or repeated is not documented; expect at most two elements but specifics are unknown.

functions.name: helpers::generateToken
functions.description: Generates and returns a token string, likely for identification or authorization. Length, character set, and uniqueness guarantees are not documented.
requirements: No inputs required.
No guarantees about entropy, format, or uniqueness are documented; do not assume cryptographic strength without inspecting implementation.

functions.name: helpers::urldecode
functions.description: Decodes a URL-encoded C-string from src into dst (e.g., converts percent-escapes and plus spaces as applicable). Writes a null-terminated decoded string to dst.
requirements: src must be a valid, null-terminated C-string.
dst must be a valid, writable buffer large enough to hold the fully decoded output including the terminating null byte.
dst and src must not be null.
Decoding rules (e.g., handling of '+', invalid percent-escapes, and character set) are not specified in the header.

functions.name: helpers::cStrCopy
functions.description: Creates and returns a C-style null-terminated copy of the given std::string. Intended for interop with C APIs requiring char*. Allocation and ownership semantics are not documented in the header.
requirements: str may be any valid std::string, including empty.
The returned pointer refers to dynamic storage; exact allocator and required deallocation routine are unknown from the header—callers must consult implementation to free correctly.
Returned pointer may be null on allocation failure (behavior not documented); callers should be prepared to handle null if implementation allows.

functions.name: helpers::hasRequiredFields
functions.description: Checks whether a JSON object contains all specified required field names. Returns true if all keys are present, false otherwise.
requirements: input is expected to be a JSON object; behavior for non-object inputs is unspecified.
keys should list required field names; interpretation is by presence only—types/values are not documented.
Key matching semantics (case sensitivity, nested paths) are not specified; assume flat, exact-name presence unless implementation indicates otherwise.

functions.name: helpers::missingRequiredField
functions.description: Returns the name of a missing required field from a JSON object if any are absent; otherwise returns an empty optional. Useful for reporting the first missing field.
requirements: input is expected to be a JSON object; behavior for non-object inputs is unspecified.
keys should list required field names; presence testing only—types/values not documented.
Order of checking and which missing key is returned if multiple are absent are not documented.

functions.name: helpers::hasField
functions.description: Checks whether a JSON object contains a field with the given name. Returns true if present, false otherwise.
requirements: input is expected to be a JSON object; behavior for non-object inputs is unspecified.
key is matched by exact name; advanced semantics (case, nesting) are not documented.

Returned list contents are platform- or configuration-dependent; specifics are unknown from the header.

requirements: mode must be a valid settings::AppMode enumerator.

Callers should not assume idempotence or whether the function modifies path in place in addition to returning a value; consult implementation if this matters.

functions.name: helpers::unNormalizePath
functions.description: Reverses prior normalization of a filesystem path, producing a form suitable for external display or specific platform conventions. Takes a non-const reference and returns the resulting path string.
requirements: path must be a modifiable std::string lvalue (non-const).
Exact transformation rules and relationship to normalizePath are not documented; behavior may be platform-dependent.

requirements: No inputs required.
Do not assume a particular format or timezone without inspecting implementation.

Details of the result type are defined in api/fs/fs.h and are unknown here.

Caller must examine fs::FileReaderResult to handle success/failure according to that type's API (inferred from return type name).
Behavior may depend on the current ResourceMode (inferred from surrounding API).

functions.name: resources::extractFile

Typically used to materialize bundled or embedded resources onto disk for external use. Exact overwrite behavior or directory creation is not specified.
requirements: filename identifies the source resource within the currently selected resource mode (inferred from API).
outputFilename is a filesystem path where the extracted content should be written; caller should ensure the target directory exists and is writable (inferred from function purpose).
